role: Acting Assistant Secretary for Environment and Urban Systems, U.S. Department of Transportation
stance_basis: memo lists four specific documentation requirements for the final EIS before the project can be considered adequate
summary: John E. Hirten, Acting Assistant Secretary for Environment and Urban Systems at the U.S. Department of Transportation, submitted a memo commenting on the draft EIS for the Lincoln Highway widening project. He expressed appreciation for the review opportunity but identified four areas requiring additional documentation in the final statement, including relocation housing, alternatives to use of Section 4(f) lands, efforts to minimize harm to the playground, and coordination with HUD and Interior on Section 4(f) lands. His support is conditional on these documentation improvements being incorporated into the final EIS.
complaint_summary: Hirten requests that the final EIS document four items: relocation housing input, alternatives to use of Section 4(f) lands (such as widening on the other side of Lincoln Highway), efforts to minimize harm to the playground including whether ballfields will be preserved or replaced, and coordination with HUD and Interior on Section 4(f) lands.

statement.text:
We appreciate the opportunity to review and comment on this draft environmental impact statement. We would suggest that the final statement document the following:
1. Input from agencies or staff with relocation expertise on whether any problems are likely to arise with respect to replacement housing.
2. It is suggested that the final statement provide documentation of alternatives to the use of 4(f) lands, such as utilizing the other side of Lincoln Highway for the widening.
3. More description of efforts to minimize harm to the playground would be helpful, including whether the existing ballfields will be preserved or replaced.
4. It would be helpful to have the final statement reflect coordination of the project with the Department of Housing and Urban Development and the Department of the Interior on the Section 4(f) lands.
We look forward to receiving the final environmental impact statement and proposed Section 4(f) determination, including the comments received from other public agencies and the general public on the draft statement.
John E. Hirten
Acting Assistant Secretary
